reference.title: The use of quartz as an internal pressure standard in high-pressure crystallography

methods.notes: Angel et al.'s room-temperature BM3 has V0=112.981(2) A^3, K0=37.12(9) GPa, and K0'=5.99(4).

recalculation.notes: Every simultaneously measured quartz conventional-cell volume and standard deviation is bundled. Using the run's 0.0001 GPa quartz volume as V0 and the Angel et al. K0 and K0' reproduces the printed pressures to 0.0044 GPa maximum residual; this run normalization removes the ambient cell-volume offset while retaining the cited calibrant compression law.

assessment.basis: Every compared free coefficient meets both the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison and parameter-specific numerical similarity screen. Error conventions and fit qualifications remain applicable.

scientific_validation.note: Validated directly against the complete free-access publisher article. No supplementary data file is listed; the official HTML exposes Tables 1 and 4-6 in full.

primary_source_check.finding: The source defines a three-free-parameter, error-weighted BM3 fit to all 11 Fe56 observations and gives the Eulerian equation, conventional-cell volume basis, exact sample composition, and quartz pressure calibration.
primary_source_check.record_note: Coefficients from paragraph 25 and Table 6: an EoSFIT error-weighted fit to all 11 Fe56 rows of Table 4, with quartz pressure calibration.

primary_data_check.finding: All 11 printed Fe56 lattice parameters, V/V0 values, simultaneous quartz volumes, reduced pressures, and parenthetical standard deviations are transcribed losslessly.

independent_refit.objective: Effective-variance pressure residuals combining tabulated pressure and lattice-parameter standard deviations; the ambient pressure has no printed standard deviation.
independent_refit.conclusion: The independent refit recovers every published coefficient within its printed standard deviation; the V0 difference is 0.98 of the printed standard deviation.

parameter_provenance.determination_method: Measurements or their experimental reduction determine this EOS; source: Paragraphs 23-26; Tables 1 and 4 and 6; Figures 5-6.
parameter_provenance.equation: Paragraphs 25-26 and Figure 6: standard third-order Birch-Murnaghan EOS in the Eulerian finite-strain convention, with f=[(V0/V)^(2/3)-1]/2 and F=P/[3f(1+2f)^(5/2)].
parameter_provenance.V0: Paragraph 25: freely fitted V0=77.453(4) A^3 for the conventional cubic cell.
parameter_provenance.K0: Paragraph 25 and Table 6: freely fitted isothermal K0=155.8(9) GPa.
parameter_provenance.K0_prime: Paragraph 25 and Table 6: freely fitted K'=5.53(23).
parameter_provenance.reference_temperature: The article reports room/ambient temperature but no numeric kelvin value; 298 K is an explicit operational reference for this isothermal record.
parameter_provenance.fit_selection: Paragraphs 24-25 and Table 4: all 11 Fe56 rows, including the zero-pressure in-cell observation.
parameter_provenance.weighting: Paragraph 25: error-weighted three-parameter fit with EoSFIT; the table supplies row-wise sample-lattice and pressure standard deviations.

superseded_record_text.notes: The EOS volume is one conventional Fm-3m rocksalt cell with four oxygen-normalized formula units. All three coefficients were fitted. The source reports standard deviations but no parameter covariance matrix or explicit confidence convention beyond that designation.
validity_notes: The bounds are the complete Table 4 measurement envelope, not a phase-stability guarantee.
The 4:1 methanol-ethanol medium and single-crystal experiment define the stress environment.
The numeric temperature is operational because the source states only room/ambient temperature.
